text.tspan: : Dot plots of morning and evening student scores.
Important! Rounding the Mean and Standard Deviation!
, we will round our results to one decimal
place more than the original data (two decimal places is also acceptable for the standard deviation).
For example, if the data are whole numbers, we should round the mean and standard deviation each
to one decimal place. If the data are rounded to one decimal place, we should round the mean and
standard deviation to two decimal places.
gives quiz scores of 9 students split into two groups, group 1, and group 2. Assume the
groups are populations. Find the population variance and population standard deviation for each group.
Which group is more widely dispersed? Which is more closely grouped?
First type or copy the data into STAT-Utility, one column for each group, and name the columns
“Group #1” and “Group #2.” Select Descriptive Statistics → Basic Statistics and check both
columns under “Columns to include.” Since we are looking for the population variance and
standard deviation, click “Select none” under “Statistics to show,” then check “Population variance
(σ²)” and “Population standard deviation (σ).” Click “Show results in a new window.”
